feedback.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=2,{x}_{2}={x}_{3}=3,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $-1.$ Find $P(x).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}={x}_{3}=3,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=-1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =-1(x-2)(x-3)(x-3) \\  & =-(x-2)(x-3)(x-3)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-(x-2)(x-3)(x-3) & =-({x}^{2}-6x+9)(x-2) \\  & =-({x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}-2{x}^{2}+9x+12x-18) \\  & =-({x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}+21x-18) \\  & =-{x}^{3}+8{x}^{2}-21x+18.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=-{x}^{3}+8{x}^{2}-21x+18.$
